subject: Invoice delivery options: tokenized email vs portal enrolment
messages:
From: Sophie Li <accounts-payable@cascadiahealth.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: ap@cascadiahealth.com
Date: 2028-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Billing delivery preference & interim flow

Hi Irene,

Quick question as we transition vendors — we'd like invoices pushed into our vendor portal long-term, but our procurement team needs a short interim for July invoices while onboarding is completed. Two asks: 1) can Redwood deliver a signed PDF via email with a machine-readable XML attachment for AP automation? and 2) if we need email for the next 6 weeks, can you include a verifiable timestamp or token so our system can auto-ingest and validate authenticity?

Also, PO matching is strict on our side (we require invoice->PO match within 7 days). If there's any chance of delay, please flag invoices and include a remittance_alias field in the XML.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Sophie Li
Senior AP Analyst
Cascadia Health

Attachment: sample_invoice_345.pdf (PDF stub), invoice_payload_345.xml (XML stub)
From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Li <accounts-payable@cascadiahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing delivery preference & interim flow

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and samples. We're happy to support a temporary email push with a verification token and the XML payload included. Options we can offer immediately: 

- Ephemeral signed PDF + embedded XML (email attachment): we include a SHA256 hash in the email header and a human-readable stamp (time + signer).
- Tokenized webhook header: we can send a one-time HMAC token in an "X-Invoice-Token" header that your ingestion layer can validate against a shared secret. Good for automated ingestion and avoids SFTP setup.
- Portal enrollment link (recommended long-term): we'll provide a one-click enrollment for your AP team; once onboarded, invoices appear in your portal and we stop email pushes.

Before we proceed: can you confirm which interim option you prefer (signed-pdf+xml OR webhook-tokened email) and the remit alias your system wants included in the XML? Also confirm the single email address for delivery (accounts-payable@cascadiahealth.com) and whether PO numbers live in the XML <POReference> tag.

If you prefer, Marissa can share a sample HMAC token generation spec and a tiny schema for the XML namespace we use.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Billing delivery preference & interim flow

Hi Sophie — looping in technical details for your AP team. We can support both flows; pros/cons below to help you decide quickly: 

1) Signed PDF + XML attachment (fastest to implement)
   - Pros: human-readable PDF for GL review + structured XML for automated import; no secrets to rotate on your side.
   - Cons: verification relies on included hash and visible stamp; slightly higher manual friction for validation on your side.

2) Tokenized email header (recommended interim for automation)
   - Pros: HMAC header validated by your ingestion service; minimal schema changes; robust against tampering in transit.
   - Cons: requires a short secret exchange (we provision an HMAC secret and you configure validation).

Implementation notes (we attached samples in the thread):
- XML will include fields: <InvoiceNumber>, <InvoiceDate>, <Amount>, <VATAmount>, <POReference>, <RemittanceAlias>.
- We will include <VATTag reverseCharge="false"> unless you ask for reverse-charge tagging.
- HMAC header name: X-RW-Invoice-Signature, algorithm: HMAC-SHA256, token format: timestamp|nonce|signature. We will publish a sample validator script (Node/Python).
- Delivery cadence: daily push at 02:00 UTC for any invoices generated previous business day. We can change to hourly if you need near-real-time.

Connor — can you attach the sample validator and a short checklist for AP onboarding?

Sophie — if you confirm tokenized header, we'll send the secret via DocuSign-equivalent secure link and start with July invoices only (we won't push prior months).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachment: validator_example.js (code stub), xml_schema_v1.xsd (schema stub)
From: Sophie Li <accounts-payable@cascadiahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-07-29T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Billing delivery preference & interim flow

Thanks, Marissa and Irene — tokenized email header sounds like the right interim approach. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Delivery address: accounts-payable@cascadiahealth.com (this is the system inbox).
- Please include <RemittanceAlias> = "CASC-INV-001" in the XML.
- POReference is present in our PO export and will be used for matching; 7-day match window is firm.
- VAT: we use reverse-charge for certain services; I'll attach a list of NACE codes that require reverse-charge by end of day tomorrow. If reverse-charge applies, set <VATTag reverseCharge="true"> and include VATAmount=0.

Next steps from Redwood: send the HMAC secret via secure link and a test invoice (PDF + XML + X-RW-Invoice-Signature header) to our sandbox address test-ap@cascadiahealth.com. We'll validate ingestion and confirm.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sophie Li
Senior AP Analyst
Cascadia Health
